extracted.intended_audience: professionals, journalists, communicators, and managers seeking to improve concise business/newsroom writing and newsletters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing concise, high-impact communications (headlines, newsletters, emails, and short-form news) using the 'Smart Brevity' approach: prioritize essentials, explain impact, and structure content for quick scanning and retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity is confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Brevity is confidence. Length is fear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as the guiding principle of Smart Brevity: prefer shorter, stronger expressions because they convey confidence and respect readers' time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize essential information and explain impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize essential news and information, explain its impact and deliver it in a concise and visual format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on what matters most to the reader and explicitly state why it matters; combine concision with visual/structural cues to make the key point stand out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write muscular headlines (six strong words or fewer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write muscular headlines, six strong words or fewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headlines should grab attention quickly and economically. (Customer reviews also warn to avoid turning headlines into deceptive clickbait.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a memorable opening sentence / 'why it matters'
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a memorable opening sentence and provide a short paragraph on 'why it matters'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with a clear, single-sentence hook that frames the importance; follow with a very short 'why it matters' explanation to orient the reader before offering details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a compact structure: headline + why_it_matters + go_deeper
rubrics_metrics.description: Format at a glance: a headline that grabs attention; a short paragraph on 'why it matters'; go deeper using some prompts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt this three-part scaffold to make content scannable and offer a clear path from summary to deeper detail for readers who want more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate fluff and gobbledygook
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cut needless words and jargon; prefer clear, plain-language sentences that convey one core idea at a time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drill your ONE thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Write clear, concise sentences; drill your ONE thought into your audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each piece or paragraph should revolve around a single primary idea—avoid packing multiple competing messages into the same short item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point readers to where they can learn more
rubrics_metrics.description: Point people to where they can learn more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise prompts, links, or next-step resources so interested readers can dive deeper without overloading the primary communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use visual chunking and bullet points
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver information in a concise and visual format; use bullet points rather than a wall of text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chunk content into bite-sized elements (bullets, subheads, blocks) to improve scanability, comprehension and retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the message audience-first
rubrics_metrics.description: Your message should be about the needs of the receiver and NOT your needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always frame content from the reader's perspective: what they need to know, why it matters to them, and what action/understanding they should take away.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for comprehension and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Present it in a way the audience will receive, comprehend, and retain it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond brevity, structure and clarity must support the reader's ability to process and remember the core point; use clear context, signposts, and minimal cognitive load.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include quick-read metadata (Smart Brevity count)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Smart Brevity™ count of the word count and the time required to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give readers an upfront indication of time cost (word count/read time) so they can decide whether to read now or come back later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create bite-sized, attention-grabbing content
rubrics_metrics.description: Create bite-sized content that gets noticed (analogized to TikTok-sized content).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short, punchy items are more likely to cut through digital noise; design for very short attention spans while still delivering the key insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be concise but preserve tone and relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Conciseness can be curt; be mindful that brevity may eschew cultural niceties and relationship-building language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Smart Brevity selectively—shortness should not unnecessarily sacrifice courtesy, nuance, or the relational cues that matter in some contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid repetition and unnecessary length
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid repetition—repetition contradicts the teaching of brevity and can make content feel longer than necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim repetitive passages and resist padding; if an idea can be communicated in fewer words, do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misleading or deceptive headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlines should not be deceptive or clickbait (critique: some suggested headlines risked deception).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be attention-grabbing without misleading readers about the substance of the content—maintain trust and accuracy even when writing brief headlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make communications inclusive and accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: Smart Brevity can make communications more inclusive for readers with dyslexia, ADHD, or for whom English is a second language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer simple vocabulary, short sentences, clear structure and chunking to increase readability and inclusivity.
